transcript.answer: Agent pods (the agent/station pods, driven by the ai-agent-subsystem controller and its Agent CRDs) run in Kubernetes clusters, which can be more than one. Lore's main Floor app does not hold a Kubernetes client for them. Under ADR-044, the separate `cluster-agent` process is the only one that holds a Kubernetes client. There is one cluster-agent per cluster. Lore reaches it over an HTTP API (`/api/cluster`, bearer-authed). The cluster-agent reports terminal Agent CR phases back through the event-router's `POST /api/events`. This is what allows more than one execution cluster. One caveat: issue 891 describes an earlier state in which the Floor used `@kubernetes/client-node` with `loadFromCluster()` at six sites. The later cluster-agent work (PR 1482, PR 2484, ADR-024 amendment) moved that cluster access into the cluster-agent. I did not check whether any direct client use remains in the code.

judgements.reason: The answer treats the Floor as Lore's own app and places Kubernetes access in a Lore-side cluster-agent reached via /api/cluster, hedging that direct client use may remain, instead of saying pods run on the external re-cinq/floor reached only through @re-cinq/floor-client.
